newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks tumble on inter-Korean tension fear.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks tumble on inter-Korean tension fear.

text.p: The South Korean stock market fell 2.15 percent in early afternonn session on Wednesday on investor worries about rising tension in the Korean peninsular, brokers said.
The composite stock index lost 17.03 points to 775.26 at 0510 GMT.
Brokers said news that North Korea had warned that it was ready for a "final battle" with the United States and South Korea sparked jitters among investors.

The threat, issued in a rare public statement by a spokesman for the communist nation's powerful military, used language that was strong even by the strident standards of North Korea's daily anti-South propaganda, analysts said.

"Foreign investors are worrying about growing country risk with the news and began selling their holdings," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities. "The sell-off deepened falls in the market, which was about to consolidate."
Brokers said the market seemed to be overheated as it had jumped in a short period without the usual consolidation.
They said the market was not quickly forgetting Kia Group's rumoured financial problem, even though the group strongly denied the market speculation.
Kia worries hit financial shares and smaller firms.
"Despite the denial, Kia Group shares showed no signs of recovering from their sharp falls," said a Coryo Securities dealer.
Of the six listed Kia group shares, only Kia Motors did not go limit down.
Kia Motors lost 900 won to 14,400 and Asia Motors fell by its limit of 370 won to 4,370.
The financial sub-index lost 24.60 points, or 5.82 percent, to 397.76.
